To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the thermoelectric conversion efficiency is not the only parameter that is relevant for the development of a thermoelectric generator, (2) skutterudites and half-Heuslers are the most promising materials for thermoelectric generator module fabrication and (3) a modular design is the most promising approach for the fabrication of thermally stable, scalable, and cost-efficient thermoelectric generator systems.

the thermoelectric materials skutterudites and half-Heuslers have already reached the performance level of the state-of-the-art thermoelectric materials for medium-high to hightemperature applications.

(1) skutterudites are a promising material class for medium-high temperature applications, (2) half-Heuslers are a promising material for medium-high to medium-high temperature applications and (3) silicon-based materials are a promising material concept for high temperature applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
materials and module designs which are both, scalable and compatible with existing fabrication technologies.
the development of a sustainable technology for the conversion of heat into electricity.
the development of thermodynamic concepts for the efficient conversion of low temperature heat into electricity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all presented material concepts have the potential to be the basis of a sustainable technology for waste heat recovery.
the thermoelectric technology is ready to take off and to be implemented in industrial applications.

there is a wide range of thermoelectric material systems, which have already reached the performance level for industrial applications, and that these materials can be processed to modules with high reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of novel thermoelectric materials and the fabrication of modules is an important and necessary first step, but not sufficient to enable a mass market for this technology.
thermoelectric heat conversion is a promising and sustainable technology for the future.

the combination of the three presented classes of materials with the discussed module design concepts may provide a basis for a sustainable and economically viable thermoelectric heat conversion technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of a new class of materials, the design and fabrication of thermoelectrics generator modules, and the design of thermoelectric heat conversion systems are all equally important for a successful implementation of this technology.

thermoelectric generator systems can become competitive with other heat-to-electric power conversion technologies if the materials are optimized and the module configuration is adapted to the respective application.
the combination of a novel thermoelectric material and a well-designed module can provide the basis for the development of a sustainable and cost-effective waste heat recovery technology.
